title: The Welch function is not third-order sum-free

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
Let n = 2m+1. Hou and Zhao conjectured that for n ≥ 7 the Welch function X2m+3 on F2n sums to zero over some three-dimensional affine subspace, that is, it is not third-order sum-free (arXiv:2609.31489, Conjecture 4.10). We prove this. For x outside F2 and u = x2m, the subspaces spanned by 1, x and a third element with zero sum exist exactly when Tr(1/(x+u)) = Tr(xu/(x+u)) = 1, so there are (2n+1−3Kn)/4 such x, where Kn is the Kloosterman sum of F2n. Weil's bound makes this positive for every n ≥ 7, and the count reproduces every value Hou and Zhao computed.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX source, arXiv tarball) and independent checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4: the criterion at every element of F2n for odd n ≤ 21, the zero-sum subspaces counted from the definition for n ≤ 11, Lean kernel checks for n = 5 and 7, and Lean 4 + Mathlib proofs of the algebraic identities of the proof.
